paragraph_text: The Beneficiary satisfies 8 C.F.R. §204.5(h)(3)(i) by demonstrating receipt of nationally and internationally recognized awards for excellence in the field. The Beneficiary was selected as a scholar of Beijing's 'Hundred People Project,' a prestigious talent recognition program that identifies and supports exceptional academics in China [Exhibit A1, p.2]. This selection demonstrates that the Beneficiary's scholarly work has been recognized at the highest levels within China's academic community, as the program specifically targets individuals who have demonstrated outstanding contributions to their fields [Exhibit A1, p.2]. The 'Hundred People Project' represents a highly competitive national-level initiative that identifies only a limited number of scholars from across China's vast academic landscape, making the Beneficiary's selection a significant achievement that distinguishes him from his peers [Exhibit A1, p.2]. Furthermore, the Beneficiary's work 'On Age' won the third prize of Outstanding Achievements in Humanities and Social Sciences of the Ministry of Education of China, a nationally recognized award established by the Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China in 2009 to reward researchers who have made outstanding contributions in the field of humanities and social sciences [Exhibit A1, p.2; Exhibit B10, p.2; Exhibit B10, p.4]. This award is administered through a rigorous evaluation process conducted every three years by an Award Committee composed of the director, deputy directors of the Social Sciences Committee of the Ministry of Education, and heads of relevant departments, with evaluation criteria requiring adherence to Marxism, theoretical innovation, and significant academic or practical contributions [Exhibit B10, p.4; Exhibit B10, p.5]. The award structure includes only four tiers—grand prizes, first prizes, second prizes, and third prizes—with the Beneficiary's third prize representing recognition among the top achievements selected from submissions across all Chinese higher education institutions [Exhibit B10, p.5]. This national-level recognition demonstrates that the Beneficiary's scholarly work has been evaluated against the highest standards in Chinese academia and found to merit distinction among the country's most significant contributions to humanities and social sciences research [Exhibit A1, p.2; Exhibit B10, p.2]. In addition to these academic honors, the Beneficiary received the Data Legacy of the Year Award at the 2019 Data Awards, which are recognized as one of the most influential awards in the field of mobile Internet in China, jointly launched by Umen+, Zhongguancun Big Data Industry Alliance, Tsingdata Big Data Industries Association, and China Big Data Industry Observation [Exhibit B1, p.2; Exhibit B3, p.2; Exhibit B3, p.3]. The selection process involved a jury of 21 judges from dozens of authorities and industry experts and scholars including China Academy of Information and Communications Technology, Tsinghua University, and Peking University, who evaluated candidates over a two-month review period using professional selection models [Exhibit B3, p.3]. From this rigorous evaluation, only 28 individuals across seven categories received Data Awards, with the Beneficiary's Data Legacy of the Year Award specifically recognizing individuals who have worked deeply in big data and mobile Internet for many years, spreading insights and experiences to educate the entire industry [Exhibit B3, p.4; Exhibit B3, p.7]. The Beneficiary's recognition places him among elite peers who received other prestigious Data Awards categories including Most Influential Award of the Year and Best Data Practice Award of the Year, demonstrating his standing at the forefront of China's data industry [Exhibit B3, p.6; Exhibit B3, p.8]. Moreover, the Beneficiary's paper titled 'Challenges Posed by the Internet to Traditional Media in the Time Dimension - A Study on the Possibility of Internet Media Usage Time Surpassing Traditional Media Usage Time' won the Excellent Paper Award at the 11th China Communication Conference, a major national conference organized by the Communication Association of China [Exhibit B11, p.2]. This recognition demonstrates that the Beneficiary's research has been evaluated and selected as outstanding by the organizing committee of a premier national communication conference, indicating peer recognition of his scholarly contributions to the field of communication studies [Exhibit B11, p.2]. The certificate was issued by both the Communication Association of China and the 11th China Communication Conference Organizing Committee, indicating formal recognition from the leading professional organization in China's communication field [Exhibit B11, p.2]. Beyond these specific awards, the Beneficiary's recognition extends beyond academic awards to include prestigious industry accolades, as evidenced by Umen+'s receipt of multiple awards including 'Enterprise Service High-growth Company 36 Kr' and 'China Big Data Industry Application TOP Choice Three Major Fields,' demonstrating the caliber of organizations that have recognized his contributions [Exhibit B4, p.4]. These industry awards recognize Umen+ as a leader in China's big data sector, with the company having received over sixty intellectual property rights and the Information System Security Level-3 Assurance Certificate issued by the Ministry of Public Security, indicating the high standards of the organizations that have recognized the Beneficiary's work [Exhibit B4, p.3]. The Beneficiary's association with an award-winning organization that has been recognized as a '2019 China Big Data Innovative Enterprises TOP 100' and received the 'Annual Best Retailing Intelligent Data Application Award' at the 14th Shanghai Retail Industry Summit further demonstrates the broad industry impact and recognition of his work across multiple sectors [Exhibit B4, p.4]. In sum, the foregoing evidence clearly establishes that the Beneficiary has received nationally and internationally recognized awards for excellence in the field.
